title: Journey - Five Days of Gratitude - Day 1: Begin with thanks

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, a soft smile in the voice, unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Five Days of Gratitude. <short pause> This is day one, Begin with Thanks. <short pause> Over these five days, we'll learn five short sentences of thanks, one at a time. <short pause> By the end, they will make one small prayer... that you can carry anywhere.

Let's start by arriving. <short pause> Set down whatever is in your hands, if you can. <short pause> Let your shoulders drop a little. <short pause> Take a breath in... <short pause> and let it go slowly. <short pause> You don't have to feel thankful yet. <short pause> You only have to be here.

When we hear the word gratitude, most of us reach for a list. <short pause> My home, my family, my health. <short pause> Those are good things to be thankful for. <short pause> But lists can get shorter. <short pause> Some days, the very thing at the top of the list is the thing that's in trouble. <short pause> So we won't begin with the gifts. <short pause> We'll begin with the Giver.

Psalm one hundred is a song of thanksgiving, for people on their way in to worship. <short pause> You can almost hear their feet on the road, and their voices getting louder as they near the gates. <short pause> These are verses four and five.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name. <short pause> For the Lord is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Did you notice the reason? <short pause> It doesn't say, for the harvest was good. <short pause> It doesn't say, for the year went well. <short pause> It says... for the Lord is good. <short pause> That was true before today began. <short pause> And it will still be true, whatever today turns out to be.

So picture a gate in front of you. <short pause> An old one, wooden, worn pale where many hands have pushed it open. <short pause> People have walked through it laughing. <short pause> People have walked through it limping. <short pause> No one is stopped, and asked how their week has been. <short pause> There is only one thing to bring with you as you step through... <short pause> and that is thanks.

parts.style: gently wondering, slow, leaving room to answer
parts.text: Before you step, choose one word for who God is. <short pause> Not something He has given you. Something He is. <short pause> Kind. <short pause> Patient. <short pause> Faithful. <short pause> Near. <short pause> It might be the word you've known to be true for years. <short pause> Or it might be the one you most need to be true today. <short pause> Take a moment, and choose yours.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now, hold that word, and walk slowly through the gate. <short pause> As you breathe in, say it silently to Him. <short pause> You are... and then your word. <short pause> As you breathe out... thank You. <short pause> Again. <short pause> You are... <short pause> Thank You. <short pause> Once more, in your own time.

parts.style: warm reassurance, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: If your word felt a little hollow just now, that's all right. <short pause> Thanks doesn't have to be felt all the way down before it counts. <short pause> Sometimes we say what is true, and the heart follows a few steps behind. <short pause> It's still coming through the gate.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: And here is the first of our five sentences. <short pause> It's the simplest, and all the others will stand on it. <short pause> You are good. <short pause> Say it with me, very quietly. <short pause> You are good.

Let's pray. <short pause> Lord, I come in through Your gate with the little thanks I have. <short pause> Before You give me anything else today, You are already good. <short pause> Your mercy doesn't run out when my feelings do. <short pause> Teach me to begin here... with You. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, warm, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: For the rest of this day, choose one doorway you often walk through. <short pause> A kitchen, a car door, the front step. <short pause> When you pass through it, let it be your gate, and say those three words. <short pause> You are good. <short pause> That's all day one asks of you. <short pause> Go gently.
